item.title: Transport v2.7.0.65
item.description:
Product: Transport v2.7.0.65
Company: Levylab
Release Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 18:20:12 -0400
Packager: Patrick Irvin

Description: VIs for scripting and performing transport measurments.

[Control Experiment]
- Control Experiment.vi
- provides a uniform way to record information about your sample & device
- record how the lockin is connected to the device
- configure the Krohn Hite amplifier
- set the base path for saving data
- configure peripheral instruments
- APIs for recording sample data, instrument status

[Transport]
Basic transport measurments:
- Lockin vs time (Lockin_time.vi)
- Lockin Sweep Mode (Lockin_sweep.vi)

[Transport Server]
Server used for scripting and performing asynchronous transport measurments.


Release Notes: ### 2.7.0

Experiments no longer stop for an error dialog, and a lock-in that is briefly unreachable no longer ends a sweep (levylabpitt/Transport#180).

- Lockin_sweep, Lockin_time and THz_TimeDelay: errors are logged to "Transport errors.log" in the experiment folder instead of opening a dialog. Brief communication errors (timeouts) are retried; any other error stops the run cleanly, saving what was acquired.
- Lockin_sweep: keeps polling through short lock-in outages and stops with error 5162 only if the lock-in does not answer for 60 s. Sweep data is read with retries.
- Lockin_sweep files now include:
- "Sweep-Data-Valid": False if the sweep data could not be read, so the file holds no sweep arrays;
- "Time-Array": the timestamp of each data point, derived from t0 and dt of the waveforms.
- Configure Experiment: opens each instrument once and keeps the connection for the session, instead of reconnecting on every poll.
- Experiment windows have a button to open the experiment folder in Explorer.
- Transport Server: experiments are started by method (LockinSweep, LockinTime, LockinTimeDelay), and their front panels can be shown or hidden.
- Transport Server front panel controls are preserved
- Deprecated: Sweep Control and Continuous B Sweep can no longer be started from the Transport Server.

Requires RemoteControl.ZMQ 1.5.4 and labview-zmq 3.7.1 (install both on every machine that runs Transport).
item.dc:creator: Levylab

item.title: Multichannel Lockin v3.8.6.97
item.description:
Product: Multichannel Lockin v3.8.6.97
Company: LevyLab
Release Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 16:00:59 -0400
Packager: Patrick Irvin

Description: Multichannel Lockin for National Instruments' Dynamic Signal Acquisition hardware (4431, 4461, 4462).
- This version is configured to handle multiple cards for simultaneous, synchronized AI/AO.
- The analog outputs can be configured to output sine, square, sawtooth, or triangle functions with (swept) DC offsets.
- Each of the analog inputs can be demodulated at multiple frequencies.

Release Notes: ### 3.8.6
Rebuilt against RemoteControl.ZMQ 1.5.4 and labview-zmq 3.7.1.
- Fixes occasional crashes ("ZeroMQ Abort" dialog, then error 1097) in the lock-in and in LabVIEW clients: labview-zmq 3.7.1 ships a libzmq built without WSAPoll (levylabpitt/RemoteControl.ZMQ#2).
- #183 getStatus replies in ~8 ms around startSweep; fixes getStatus timeouts during Transport sweeps (requires RemoteControl.ZMQ 1.5.4 and labview-zmq 3.7.1)
- #184 Improved DAQmx error classification (recoverable vs. fatal errors)
- #185 setSweepTable, and the sweep-pattern table in the UI, applied only the last table when several channels were given one; all tables are applied now. New method names setSweepTime and setSweepTable; setSweep_Time and setSweep_Table still work but are deprecated.
Machines that run Transport, FLEX or other clients need RemoteControl.ZMQ 1.5.4 and labview-zmq 3.7.1 installed too; the crash fix only applies where they are installed.
item.dc:creator: LevyLab
